newsitem.title: USA: CME spot live cattle close up, others mostly lower.
newsitem.headline: CME spot live cattle close up, others mostly lower.

text.p: Spot August CME live cattle futures closed stronger on recent gains in fed cattle prices and a stronger tone to boxed beef values while back months were uneven ahead of Friday's USDA cattle report. Feeder cattle continued to be influenced by price swings in corn futures, traders said.

Live cattle closed 0.300 cent per lb higher to 0.150 lower with August up most at 66.575 cents and October off 0.025 at 69.825 cents. Feeder cattle ended off 0.075 to up 0.300 with only August off and October up 0.025 at 80.850 cents.

Spot live cattle were underpinned by active feedlot trade at $65 per cwt Wednesday, up $1 for the week. Cattle sales in Kansas direct trade were near a one-day record at 83,000 head on Wednesday. The record figure for daily sales was set in September, 1995 at 88,000.
Higher boxed beef values quoted at midday also buoyed August into the close, they said.
USDA said boxed beef values gained $0.79 to $0.25 per cwt.
Back months drifted before Friday afternoon's monthly USDA Cattle-on-Feed report. Wide placement estimates, running on both sides of previous-year levels, kept the market nervous, traders noted.
Fund selling weighed on October early but lacked followthrough interest, they added.

Analysts' estimates for July cattle placements into feedyards in the seven key states with capacities of 1,000 head or more, averaged 100.8 percent of a year earlier and ranged from 96 to 106.5 percent. On-feed estimates averaged 115.6 percent of a year earlier and ranged from 114 to 117.8 percent and July marketings averaged 105.5 percent and ranged from 103 to 107 percent of a year ago.
Rosenthal Collins and Refco bought August while RBH sold. RBH also pressured October while R.J. O'Brien bought, pit sources said.
In live cattle options, commission houses sold the 68/71 October strangle and commercials did December risk reversal, buying 70 puts and selling 74 calls, pit sources added.
Feeder cattle were again influenced by price swings in corn futures with late local buying supporting most feeder months at the close, traders said.
The latest CME feeder cattle index, a barometer of cash feeder cattle prices, was off $0.20 at $81.19 per cwt.

LIT division of First Options spread long October short August and Cargill Investor Services spread long January feeders/short June live cattle and long August feeders/short December live cattle, pit sources said.
Boneless beef and trimmings futures closed mostly lower, again depressed by weaker cash beef markets, traders said.
Boneless beef prices this week are slipping under 90 cents per lb.
Trimmings prices ranged under 42 cents, under current futures levels, traders said.

Local and commission house selling weighed on the market with Term Commodities buying August boneless and Cargill Investor Services sold. Rosenthal Collins and Lind-Waldock sold October boneless and Term sold February. Locals and commission houses also pressured trimmings with RBH a notable seller April, pit sources said.
Boneless beef closed 1.00 cent per lb lower to 0.10 higher with August off most at 92.40 cents. Trimmings ended 0.10 higher to 1.00 lower with August off 0.80 at 44.20 cents.
